messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

**Pricing**

Every tier reads the whole diff, top to bottom. The difference between them is how many people you have and where the code sits.

**Solo — $0**
Public repos, one seat, the full rule set. No trial clock, no card. If you're a maintainer triaging drive-by pull requests at 1am, take this one. It stays free.

**Team — $19 per active author / month**
Private repos, no seat cap, and we bill only for people who actually pushed that month. Inline comments land roughly 90 seconds after a push. Rule config lives as a file in the repo, so you have the trailing-comma argument once rather than every sprint. Slack and Linear hooks included.

You also get 30 days of history: every comment we left, plus whether anyone did anything about it. That second column is the awkward one. If 4% of our comments get acted on, we'd rather you saw the number and turned checks off than kept paying for noise.

**Self-hosted — from $12,000 / year**
Runs in your VPC. Code never leaves your network, which is usually the whole security review in one sentence. Point it at your own model endpoint or use ours. SAML, audit logs, and a shared channel with an actual engineer in it instead of a ticket form.

Annual billing takes 20% off Team. Downgrading is a button, not a thread with sales, and the prorated difference lands back the same day.

**Pricing**

All three tiers read the entire diff, line by line. What changes between them is headcount and where your code lives.

**Solo — $0**
One seat, public repos, every rule turned on. No card, no countdown. If you're a maintainer sorting drive-by pull requests at 1am, this is the one. It stays free.

**Team — $19 per active author / month**
Private repos, unlimited seats, and the bill only counts people who pushed something that month. Comments show up inline about 90 seconds after a push. Your rule config is a file in the repo, so the trailing-comma argument happens once instead of every sprint. Slack and Linear hooks are in the box.

There's also 30 days of history: what we flagged, and whether anybody fixed it. The second column is the uncomfortable one. If 4% of our comments lead to a change, we'd rather you saw that and switched checks off than kept paying for noise.

**Self-hosted — from $12,000 / year**
Runs inside your VPC. Your code never crosses the network boundary, which tends to be the entire security review right there. Point it at your own model endpoint or use ours. SAML, audit logs, and a shared channel staffed by an engineer rather than a ticket form.

Pay annually and Team drops 20%. Downgrading is a button, not a thread with sales, and the prorated difference shows up the same day.
